title: Characterizing the Accuracy of ALMA Linear-polarization Mosaics
question: How accurate are ALMA linear-polarization observations away from the pointing center, and how much do mosaics of overlapping pointings reduce the residual off-axis errors

data.angular_resolution: Orion-KL synthesized beams 1.43'' x 0.95'' (Band 3) and 0.65'' x 0.48'' (Band 6)
data.sensitivity: Theoretical Stokes I sensitivity per pointing ~30 uJy/beam (Band 3, 7 min per field) and ~79 uJy/beam (Band 6, 2.2 min per field)

what.value: Archival 1.3 mm CARMA full-polarization mosaic of Orion-KL

evidence.quote: Another mosaicked polarization observation of Orion-KL was performed by (cite: Hull2014)

what.value: On-axis ALMA polarization angle uncertainty of ~0.4 deg used as a reference level

evidence.quote: on-axis uncertainty of $\sim$ 0.4$\degree$ in the polarization angle calculated by (cite: Nagai2016)

recipe.method: Use the on-axis scans of 3C 279 to solve gains, cross-hand delay, XY-phase (ambiguity-resolved with xyamb) and D-terms with the standard ALMA polarization scheme
key_parameters: Cross-hand delay solved on the scans where the XX/YY ratio changes fastest
Three executions spaced ~1 hr give parallactic angle coverage for D-terms and XY-phase
assumptions: Initial unpolarized source model for 3C 279, then polarization model from qufromgain and xyamb

recipe.goal: apply on-axis calibration to all pointings and self-calibrate
recipe.method: Apply on-axis tables to all on- and off-axis data, then one round of phase-only self-calibration per pointing
key_parameters: D-terms and XY-phase solved from on-axis data only, to mimic standard ALMA polarization calibration

recipe.goal: image Stokes I,Q,U,V and measure peaks
recipe.method: Make I,Q,U,V images with clean and extract peak values with imfit

recipe.goal: derive off-axis error maps in Q, U, chi and Pfrac
recipe.method: Divide off-axis Q and U by off-axis I, subtract the on-axis values to get dQ and dU, and take on- versus off-axis differences for chi and Pfrac
assumptions: Circular, azimuthally symmetric primary beam in Stokes I

recipe.method: Standard ALMA polarization calibration with J0522-3627 as polarization calibrator, J0423-0120 bandpass calibrator and J0529-0519 gain calibrator
key_parameters: Bandpass scan taken only in the first execution of each session

recipe.goal: image each Orion-KL mosaic pattern separately
recipe.method: Image Hyper-Nyquist, Super-Nyquist, Nyquist and single-field subsets independently with tclean, Stokes I, Q, U cleaned separately, then primary-beam correct and form P, Pfrac, chi
assumptions: Primary beam of each pointing is a 2D Gaussian peaked at the pointing center

recipe.goal: compare mosaics with the inner 1/3 FWHM of single pointings in I, Q, U
recipe.method: Build difference maps (mosaic minus single pointing) with immath, with and without a 5 sigma cutoff, and extract the inner 1/3 FWHM with imsubimage

recipe.goal: compare polarization angle in mosaic versus single pointings
recipe.method: Difference maps of chi (Hyper-Nyquist mosaic minus single pointing) for the Band 3 data, histogrammed in the inner 1/3 FWHM and the outer donut, plus median differences in high-SNR patches
key_parameters: 5 sigma_P cutoff in the chi maps

recipe.goal: compare ALMA mosaics with archival CARMA mosaic
recipe.method: Match uv-range and beam of ALMA Nyquist mosaics to CARMA, regrid to CARMA coordinates, then difference chi
assumptions: Optically thin dust with grain alignment by radiative torques, so inferred field orientation is frequency independent

recipe.goal: estimate mosaic errors from the 11x11 data
recipe.method: Standard error propagation from sigma_Q and sigma_U measured in the ring 1/3 FWHM < r < FWHM, versus direct standard deviation of the dPfrac and dchi maps
assumptions: sigma_Q approximately equals sigma_U equals sigma_P; no position-dependent error in Stokes I

answer_key.quantity: Residual Pfrac and chi errors inside inner 1/3 FWHM (3C 279, all bands)

evidence.quote: the residual errors in $P_\textrm{frac}$ and $\chi$ are $\lesssim$ 0.001 ($\lesssim$ 0.1% of Stokes $I$) and $\lesssim$ 1$\degree$, respectively

answer_key.quantity: Pfrac and chi errors near the FWHM of the primary beam (3C 279, all bands)

evidence.quote: Near the FWHM, the errors increase to $\sim$ 0.003–0.005 ($\sim$ 0.3–0.5% of Stokes $I$) and $\sim$ 1–5$\degree$, respectively

answer_key.quantity: Stokes V beam squint amplitude relative to on-axis Stokes I

evidence.quote: Each Stokes $V$ map exhibits a double-lobed “beam squint” pattern at the 1–2% level of the on-axis Stokes $I$ value

answer_key.quantity: Stokes I dynamic range in 3C 279 maps

evidence.quote: in the Stokes $I$ continuum maps ranges from $\sim$ 10,000–100,000
which had $P_\textrm{frac} \approx 12\%$ at the time of observation

answer_key.quantity: Orion-KL median polarization fraction in mosaics (Bands 3 and 6)

evidence.quote: The mosaicked images of Orion-KL at both Bands 3 and 6 have median levels of $P_\textrm{frac} \approx 6-7\%$ across the maps.

answer_key.quantity: Median SNR across the Orion-KL P maps (Bands 3 and 6)

evidence.quote: the median SNR values across the $P$ maps at Bands 3 and 6 are between 7–8

answer_key.quantity: Std of chi differences in outer donut, single pointings 6 and 10 vs Hyper-Nyquist mosaic (Band 3)

evidence.loc: Comparison of chi in the mosaics versus the inner region and outer donut region of single pointings

answer_key.quantity: Median chi difference when emission is viewed off-axis (near FWHM of point 8) versus Hyper-Nyquist mosaic

evidence.loc: Comparison of chi in the mosaics versus the inner region and outer donut region of single pointings
evidence.quote: the median difference with respect to the Hyper-Nyquist mosaic is $\sim$ 3$\degree$

answer_key.quantity: chi differences in inner 1/3 FWHM, Hyper-Nyquist mosaic vs single pointings (Band 3)
Width of ALMA minus CARMA chi difference distribution (68% window)

evidence.quote: with a width (defined as the minimum window necessary to encompass 68% of the data) of $\pm$ 12$\degree$

not_stated_but_needed: Cell size, image size, masks, threshold, niter and deconvolver for clean/tclean in both datasets (only 'standard imaging parameters' given)
Which fields and scans were treated as on-axis, and the self-calibration solution interval for the 3C 279 data
CASA version used for calibration (only imaging versions are given)
Which pointings of each 11x11 grid and which Orion-KL pointings were combined for each statistic, and exact pixel-selection regions for the inner 1/3 FWHM and donut
Primary-beam FWHM values adopted per band for the inner and donut radii
Exact definition of the polarization-angle error cutoffs applied in the 11x11 error maps
Flux values and Stokes model assumed for the polarization calibrator J0522-3627 in the Orion-KL reduction
missing_for_reproduction: Full clean/tclean parameter set (cell, image size, masks, thresholds)
Region and pointing selections for statistics
Numeric values for the Q/U/chi error maps are only in figures
score_reason: Public EOC data and public reduction scripts exist, key task versions and calibrators are given, and results are numeric, but imaging parameters and region choices are not spelled out in the paper.
rediscovery_reason: Data and scripts are public, the recipe is largely described, and the main results are numeric error levels; the work is data-heavy.
